findings.title: OAuth `state` is the static pipeline signature, so the new identity check can be bypassed
findings.body: `OAuthLoginView` sends `state=pipeline.signature` to GitHub and then validates `request.GET["state"] == pipeline.signature` (line 412). `Pipeline.signature` is an md5 of the fully-qualified class names of the pipeline views, i.e. a value that is identical for every user and every session (the new test even hard-codes it as `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). It is therefore not a per-session nonce and provides no CSRF/session binding: an attacker who authorizes the GitHub OAuth app themselves can hand a victim a URL such as `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker_code>&state=<known_signature>`. The victim's pipeline will accept it, exchange the attacker's code, and bind `github_authenticated_user` to the attacker's login — which then matches `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` and defeats exactly the installer-identity check this PR adds. Follow the existing pattern in `sentry.identity.oauth2` (`OAuth2LoginView` generates `secrets.token_hex()`, binds it with `pipeline.bind_state("state", ...)`, and `OAuth2CallbackView` compares it with `constant_time_compare`).

findings.title: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` can raise KeyError and return a 500
findings.body: The new check indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` unconditionally. `sender` is only written by `build_integration` when the incoming state contains it (currently only the GitHub `installation` webhook path), so integrations created before that metadata existed, or by any flow where the webhook did not supply a sender, have no `sender` key. In that case the installation pipeline raises `KeyError` and the user gets an unhandled 500 instead of the intended "Invalid installation request." dialog. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` (and fail closed) instead.

findings.title: Installer-identity check is skipped when the Integration row does not yet exist
findings.body: The comparison between `github_authenticated_user` and the installing GitHub user only happens in the branch where an `Integration` row already exists (lines 493-505). If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist` the pipeline immediately advances (line 482) and `build_integration` creates the integration with no identity validation at all. Since that row is created asynchronously by the GitHub `installation` webhook, an attacker who completes the Sentry pipeline before the webhook is processed (or on an instance where the webhook is not delivered) still gets the previous, unvalidated behaviour. Consider validating the authenticated user against the installation data returned by `get_installation_info()` (e.g. the account/sender) in that path as well, so the protection does not depend on a webhook race.

findings.title: Unhandled exception from `get_user_info` / `safe_urlopen` yields a 500 instead of the error dialog
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` performs an HTTP call and raises on non-2xx responses (`raise_for_status`), and `safe_urlopen` on line 423 can raise on network/timeout errors. Neither is wrapped in a try/except, so a transient GitHub failure or a revoked/invalid token during installation surfaces as an unhandled 500 in the setup popup rather than the `github-integration-failed.html` dialog that the rest of this view carefully returns. Wrap both calls and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure (ideally with logging so these failures are diagnosable).

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests installation-not-found
findings.body: The test still stubs a 404 for `/app/installations/{id}` but now passes `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match the pipeline signature used everywhere else in this file (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). The request therefore fails in `OAuthLoginView` on the state check and the assertion only verifies the generic "Invalid installation request." message. The previously covered behaviour — `build_integration` raising `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")` for a 404 from GitHub — is now untested, and nothing covers the missing-`access_token` or user-mismatch-in-OAuthLoginView branches separately. Use the correct state so the test reaches `GitHubInstallation`/`build_integration`, and add a distinct test for the state-mismatch path.

findings.title: Authorize URL built by string interpolation without URL-encoding
findings.body: `client_id`, `state` and `redirect_uri` are interpolated raw into the authorize URL. `redirect_uri` comes from `absolute_uri(...)` and can contain characters that must be percent-encoded in a query value (e.g. when the install URL carries a query string or when a custom `SENTRY_URL_PREFIX`/subdomain introduces reserved characters), which would silently corrupt the redirect GitHub uses. Build the query with `urlencode({...})` as `OAuth2LoginView` does.

findings.title: `_(error_short)` cannot be extracted for translation
findings.body: `error()` calls `_(error_short)` on a runtime variable. The literal strings passed by callers ("Invalid installation request.", "GitHub installation pending deletion.", "Github installed on another Sentry organization.") are no longer wrapped in `_()` at their definition sites, so `makemessages` will not extract them and they will never be translated (the long messages are correctly marked, the short ones are not). Mark the short strings with `gettext_lazy` at the call sites and drop the runtime `_()`.
